question.text: The conflict spread when Germany attacked this neutral country hoping to capture Liege ("leezh") and outflank the French. Instead, Britain entered the war on the Allied side.
question.clue: During WWI, this country stalled Germany at the Battle of Liege after being invaded as part of the Schlieffen Plan.

swap.leadin: This European country was the original home of the British king William of Orange.
swap.text: Name this country, which contains cities like The Hague, Rotterdam, and Amsterdam.
swap.clue: This European country traded at Dejima under the policy of sakoku , which made it the only Western nation to trade with Japan for over two hundred years.

question.text: In 1637 the Dutch economy was harmed by the sudden price collapse of these flowers whose species include Bokhara and Viceroy.
question.clue: This item names a twelve-year period overseen by Ibrahim Pasha that saw the rise of a culture-minded Ottoman nobility, who sought status by cultivating it.

swap.text: This operation attempted to capture bridges in the Netherlands using paratroopers and saw the British First Airborne Division meet heavier opposition than planned while trying to cross the Rhine River, crushing Allied hopes of ending the war by Christmas of 1944.
swap.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

question.leadin: Name the following about the European origins of the Black Legend.
question.text: This port city was subject to the 1576 "Spanish Fury" by unpaid mutinying soldiers. The collective response by the United Provinces to its destruction intensified the Eighty Years War.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.text: This Dutch noble was the main leader of the Dutch independence struggle. Philip II's offer of 25,000 crowns led this man to be eventually assassinated by Balthasar Gerard.
swap.answerHtml: William the Silent [accept William I, Prince of Orange]
swap.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the military accomplishments of European dukes.
question.text: The Duke of Alba established the "Council of Blood" during this war, the revolt of the Spanish Netherlands against Philip II of Spain.
question.clue: The first assassination of a head of state by handgun was carried out by Balthasar Gerard during this war.

swap.text: The Treaty of Munster ended the Eighty Years' War and gave this nation independence. This country allied with Sweden during the war and was led by Maurice and Frederick Henry.
swap.clue: A force from this country was defeated in a siege by a man who was born to a member of the Tagawa family and would go on to become the first ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning.

question.text: During Peter's Grand Embassy, he worked as a carpenter for this company in Saardam. This company set up a base in Jakarta in 1619.
question.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [or Dutch East Indies Company; or United East India Company; or Vereenigde Oost-indische Compagnie]
question.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an abdicated king.
swap.text: In 2004, Prince Johan Friso abdicated his claim of succession in this country due to past associates between his wife Mabel Wisse Smit and an accused drug lord.
swap.clue: This country used a defensive Water Line to halt an invasion in its "disaster year," during which a new stadtholder was chosen.

question.text: The Eighty Years War was sparked by a rebellion led by William the Silent, a member of this Dutch royal house.
question.clue: A group supported by this dynasty that adopted crescent-shaped symbols for Ottoman support was the Sea Beggars.

swap.text: The Ever Given was destined for this Dutch port, the busiest in Europe.
swap.clue: In retaliation for the German attack on this city, the RAF began the bombing of industrial facilities in the Ruhr.

question.leadin: During the French Revolutionary Wars, this region lent its name to a campaign that included the Battle of Caesar's Camp.
question.text: Name this region that gives its name to a 1792 to 1795 campaign during the War of the First Coalition. This region's port of Bruges ("broozh") historically traded wool with England.
question.answerHtml: Flanders [or Vlaaanderen; or Flandre; or Flandern; accept Flanders Campaign; accept West Flanders; accept East Flanders; accept County of Flanders; prompt on Belgium]
question.clue: One ruler of this region was imprisoned with his two sons for attempting to ally with Edward Longshanks due to this region's prominence in the wool trade.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about important figures in the history of geography.
swap.text: This Belgian-born cartographer is known today for his namesake style of projection, which distorts the poles.
swap.clue: This Flemish geographer created a 1569 world map that represented sailing courses as straight lines and distorted Greenland to the size of Africa.

question.text: This woman was the queen of the Netherlands during the war. She fled to Great Britain during the occupation and broadcast messages of inspiration to the Dutch resistance movement.

swap.leadin: At the confederal level, the holder of this position in Holland received the title of Captain-General of the army and Admiral-General of the navy.
swap.text: Name these governors of provinces including Friesland ("FREEZ-lont") and Utrecht. Orangists supported hereditary succession for this position, which they finally succeeded in amalgamating into a general form across all provinces in 1747.
swap.answerHtml: stadtholder [or stadtholder-general; or General Stadtholder; or stadhouder; or erfstadhouder; or stadhouder-generaal]
swap.clue: Reforms to pike and shot tactics made by a holder of this office directly inspired those made by Gustavus Adolphus.

question.text: In order to open shipping into Antwerp, dikes in this province were breached by the Allies to dislodge Nazi forces during Operation Infatuate. The 1953 North Sea flood devastated this province, leading to the construction of the Delta Works in it.

swap.leadin: The RAF and US Army Air Forces attempted to alleviate this event by organizing food drops termed Operation Manna and Operation Chowhound.
swap.text: Name this massive famine that took place in German-occupied Netherlands at the end of World War II.

question.leadin: After the Peace of Westphalia, the newly-independent Dutch Republic was ruled by a faction of urban merchants, in particular those based in Amsterdam.
question.text: All of that ended in 1672, the Rampjaar or disaster year, when this man was deposed after twenty-five years as Grand Pensionary and then lynched after French forces advanced through the Spanish Netherlands as far as Utrecht.
question.clue: In order to focus on his country's invasion in the War of Devolution, this man quickly negotiated the Treaty of Breda to end a war with England.

swap.leadin: A sack of this city, which led Romain Rolland to call the Germans "descendants of Attila the Hun," was preceded by a similar action undertaken by Max von Hausen's army in Dinant.
swap.text: A chapter of The Guns of August details the burning of a university library in what city by invading German forces?
